chunks: Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn Mahbub narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from 'Abd Allah ibn al-Mughirah, from Ibn Muskan, from Husayn ibn Hammad, from Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said:

I said to him: I place my face down for sajdah, and my face lands on a stone or on an elevated spot; should I move my face to a level place? He said: Yes, drag your face along the ground without lifting it.

key_terms.السُّجُودِ: sajdah; the act of prostration in salat (prayer)
key_terms.الْأَرْضِ: the ground; the surface upon which the adjustment is made
key_terms.تَرْفَعَهُ: lift it; meaning not to raise the face while correcting the position
key_terms.جُرَّ: drag; the instruction to move the face along the ground
key_terms.حَجَرٍ: a stone; an obstacle or uneven surface encountered during sajdah
key_terms.مَكَانٍ مُسْتَوٍ: a level place; an even surface to which one may adjust during sajdah
key_terms.مَوْضِعٍ مُرْتَفِعٍ: an elevated place; a raised spot unsuitable for proper prostration position
key_terms.وَجْهِي: my face; here referring to the face being placed down in prostration

ai.seo_question: What should a person do in sajdah if the forehead lands on a raised or uneven spot?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding sajdah when the forehead lands on an uneven or elevated place. The Imam عليه السلام permits moving the face to a level spot, but instructs that it should be done by dragging it along the ground without lifting it.
